sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: RSpec is the dominant testing framework in the Rails ecosystem, and interviews at Rails companies test it specifically — not just generic testing concepts. The two most important RSpec-specific questions are the let vs let! distinction (let is lazy and memoised; let! is eager and runs before the example) and shared examples for DRY contract testing. This page covers the full RSpec toolkit at the intermediate level: shared_examples_for and it_behaves_like, shared_context with include_context, custom matchers with RSpec::Matchers.define, aggregate_failures for multiple assertions without early exit, have_enqueued_job and have_enqueued_mail for async assertions, and the Rails integration setup — the difference between spec_helper.rb and rails_helper.rb and when to use each.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: rspec-structure, shared-examples, custom-matchers, rails-integration. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
